extracted.intended_audience: product designers, inventors, patent attorneys, IP law firms, and patent illustrators seeking USPTO-compliant design patent drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation of USPTO-compliant design patent drawings that constitute the entire legal disclosure of a design patent application, including required views, surface shading, broken-line strategy, sheet/margin formatting, and delivery of examiner-ready files. Guidance covers U.S. rules (37 CFR § 1.84, 37 CFR § 1.152, MPEP § 1503.02) and international/Hague considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings constitute the entire legal disclosure (the claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under MPEP § 1503.02 and 35 U.S.C. § 171, the drawing disclosure is 'the most important element of the application' and 'the drawing is the claim.' There is no written description of the design — only the illustration defines what is protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every line, surface, view, and broken line directly determines the scope of protection. Nothing should be left to conjecture; the drawings must provide a complete disclosure of the appearance of the design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with governing rules (37 CFR § 1.84, 37 CFR § 1.152, MPEP § 1503.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: All design patent drawings must meet the general drawing standards of 37 CFR § 1.84 and the design-specific requirements of 37 CFR § 1.152 and MPEP § 1503.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings should be reviewed against every applicable requirement before filing; SNS reviews against the full requirements to avoid formal drawing objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required views — sufficient number to constitute a complete disclosure (minimum seven standard views)
rubrics_metrics.description: For most three-dimensional articles a minimum of seven standard views is required: perspective, front, rear, left side, right side, top, and bottom. Views must be head-on (orthographic) rather than angled, except the single perspective figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some views may be omitted only if explicitly justified in the specification (e.g., rear identical to front, top flat and devoid of ornamentation). All visible surfaces must be accounted for to avoid § 112 rejections for insufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective view
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-dimensional view showing the overall appearance and spatial relationships of the design; provides intuitive understanding of the complete design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as the single three-dimensional figure; other orthographic views must be head-on. Perspective is typically FIG. 1 and is important for visual context but does not replace required orthographic views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front view (primary face)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary face of the article shown straight-on; typically the most important view and often selected for publication on the patent face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must clearly show the ornamental features of the design; ensure it is consistent with other views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rear view
rubrics_metrics.description: The back of the article shown directly head-on; required to disclose the complete ornamental appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be omitted only if the specification confirms the rear is identical or a mirror image of the front with an appropriate statement in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left and right side views
rubrics_metrics.description: Left and right sides of the article shown directly head-on and must show all visible surface ornamentation and contours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either may be omitted only if the side is a mirror image of the other and an appropriate specification statement is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top and bottom views
rubrics_metrics.description: Top shown directly from above and bottom shown directly from below to disclose ornamentation or surface features on those faces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be omitted if the face is flat and devoid of ornamentation, provided an explicit specification statement confirms this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental & special views allowed but limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectional views may be included to show the external contour (not internal construction). Additional perspective views, enlarged detail views, and alternate embodiment figures may be included as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include internal construction. Use supplemental figures to clarify external contours or details that orthographic views cannot fully convey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface shading — mandatory and technique-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate and adequate surface shading must be used to show the character and contour of all surfaces in three-dimensional designs (per MPEP § 1503.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Straight-line shading indicates flat surfaces; curved-line shading indicates contoured surfaces; stippling (dots) is used for curved or rounded surfaces; oblique line shading for transparent/translucent/highly polished/reflective surfaces; contrast between materials may use line shading in one area and stippling in another. Solid black is NOT permitted except to represent the color black or color contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of missing or inadequate surface shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of appropriate surface shading in the drawings as filed may result in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) for lack of enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding surface shading after the filing date may be treated as new matter under 35 U.S.C. § 132(a) and often is not permitted. Get shading correct at filing to avoid irreversible issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken lines — disclaims environmental structure and affects claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines show environmental structure or context that forms no part of the claimed design; solid lines show claimed elements. Every use of broken lines must be explained in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broken lines may NOT be used to show hidden planes or internal surfaces; alternate positions shown by full and broken lines in the same view are NOT permitted. Strategic choices about broken vs. solid lines directly impact claim breadth (more broken lines = potentially broader scope) and must be coordinated with counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain broken-line uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines may NOT be used to show hidden planes or surfaces that cannot be seen through opaque materials; alternate positions of a component shown by full and broken lines in the same view are NOT permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always accompany broken-line usage with a specification explanation. Misuse can create ambiguity and damage enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings and photographs rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings are permitted without a petition, but if color is included it becomes an integral part of the claimed design. Photographs may be used in lieu of ink drawings but cannot be combined with black-and-white line drawings in the same application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners generally recommend black-and-white line drawings unless color is essential. Photographs must not show environmental structure and have limitations for strategic shading/broken-line use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper, sheet size & margin formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing sheets must be either 8.5 × 11 inches or A4, white, smooth, non-shiny, durable. Minimum margins: top 1 inch, left 1 inch, right 5/8 inch, bottom 3/8 inch. All figures must fit within the usable surface defined by these margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure figures are entirely inside usable area; nonconforming sheets or margins can result in formal objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthographic views must be head-on (no angled orthographic views)
rubrics_metrics.description: Orthographic views (front, rear, sides, top, bottom) must be shown straight-on and not from an angle; only the designated perspective figure may use a three-dimensional angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing orthographic views from an angle is a common objection; prepare true head-on orthographic figures to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure descriptions and specification linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include figure descriptions identifying each figure by name and view type and must explain any use of broken lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing figure descriptions is a common rejection. Provide complete figure descriptions ready for incorporation into the specification to prevent this objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between views
rubrics_metrics.description: All views must be consistent — features must match across figures; inconsistencies (even minor asymmetries) can cause a § 112 rejection for indefiniteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare all views from the same master reference and cross-check for dimensional and geometric consistency to avoid indefiniteness objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: No improper use of solid black shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Solid black shading is prohibited for general shading; it may only be used to represent the color black or color contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrators must avoid using solid black for contour shading. Improper solid black usage is a common formal objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference numerals not required for design drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike utility patent drawings, reference numerals are not required for design patent drawings because there are no written claims needing reference support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include unnecessary reference numerals in design drawings; if preparing coordinated utility drawings, include numerals where required for utility claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverable file formats and examiner-ready files
rubrics_metrics.description: Final drawings should be delivered electronically in formats required for filing: PDF (for USPTO Patent Center) and high-resolution TIFF, along with a complete set of figure descriptions suitable for the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare files to be USPTO-ready to avoid filing delays; include high-resolution and correct formatting per Patent Center requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: International/Hague System differences (broken lines, color, views)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key differences exist between USPTO and international offices: many foreign offices do not permit broken lines; requirements for surface shading and color acceptance vary by country; number of views and acceptable formats differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking international protection, prepare alternate drawing sets (e.g., show previously-broken features in solid lines) and tailor drawings to the destination office's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common drawing objections to anticipate and prevent
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent objections include: environmental structure shown in solid lines, missing figure descriptions, views shown at angles rather than head-on, improper solid black shading, insufficient number of views, improper use of broken lines, inconsistencies between views, and missing or inadequate surface shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality review processes should specifically check for each of these issues. Remedies include using broken lines for contextual/environmental elements, providing complete figure descriptions, ensuring orthographic head-on views, correct shading techniques, and cross-checking view consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic broken-line usage affects claim breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing what to show in broken lines versus solid lines is a strategic decision: more broken lines can yield broader claim scope but requires careful drafting and specification language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with patent counsel to balance claiming scope and enforceability; deliberate broken-line strategy should be determined before preparing the drawing set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid introducing new matter post-filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections that add shading or views after filing risk being treated as new matter under 35 U.S.C. § 132(a) and may not be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completeness and accuracy at filing. If changes are needed after filing, expect significant legal limitations and potential inability to add omitted disclosure.
